title: Why You Must Say Sorry To Every Door
sources: Original fiction (SCIFI world-rule). Real idea used loosely: a Venus flytrap snaps shut when its trigger hairs are touched (Royal Botanic Gardens Kew; Smithsonian).

lines.text: Always say sorry to the door.
On this planet, you must apologize to every door before you open it.
Every single one.
I'm Pip.
I say sorry to the front door.
The school door.
The fridge door.
Even the toilet door, because he's very sensitive.
Then a tourist arrived. Rex.
He took one look and laughed.
Sorry, door? Doors are wood, you weirdo!
I stayed calm. I didn't explain.
So Rex kicked the school door open.
The door gasped.
He slammed the fridge.
Something inside yelled, rude!
He shouted at the town gate, move it, door!
And the gate rolled its eyes.
It actually rolled its eyes.
You see, every door here is a snap plant.
Like a flytrap that closes when you poke it,
but shy, and with feelings.
Then Rex tried the bus door.
It folded him up like a sandwich,
lifted him over the whole town,
and held him there for three hours.
He only came down when he sang sorry.
Loudly. Eleven times.
Now Rex bows to every door.
So, always say sorry to the door.
